title: Entered Apprentice: the initiation ceremony
summary: Read the complete supplied initiation dialogue and stage directions.

sections.heading: Admission, questions and prayer
sections.body:
The Ceremony of Initiation
(The Junior Deacon should be ready to prompt all answers throughout the ceremony.)
(The Brethren, to the number of not less than seven, being assembled, and the Lodge being opened in the First Degree, the Tyler sounds an Alarm; not the regular E.A. knocks but one loud knock. )
I. G. - (advances with step and sign of E.A. ) Bro. Junior Warden, there is an Alarm.
J. W. - (rises with step and sign of E.A., but no knock) Worshipful Master, there is an Alarm. (J.W. holds sign)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, you will inquire who seeks admission. (J.W. discharges sign and sits down)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds with and holds sign of E.A.) you will see who seeks admission.
(I.G. opens the door, and addresses the Tyler.)
I. G. - Whom have you there?
TY. - Mr. A. B., a poor Candidate in a state of darkness who has been well and worthily recommended, regularly proposed and approved in open Lodge, and who now comes, of his own free will and accord, properly prepared, humbly soliciting to be admitted to the mysteries and privileges of antient Freemasonry.
I. G. - How does he hope to obtain those privileges?
TY. - By the help of God, being a free man and of good report.
I. G. - Let him wait, while I report to the Worshipful Master.
(I.G. closes the door.)
I. G. (advances with step and sign of E.A., and holds the sign) -
Worshipful Master, at the door of the Lodge stands Mr. A. B., a poor Candidate in a state of darkness who has been well and worthily recommended, regularly proposed and approved in open Lodge, and who now comes, of his own free will and accord, properly prepared, humbly soliciting to be admitted to the mysteries and privileges of antient Freemasonry.
W. M. - How does he hope to obtain those privileges?
I. G. - By the help of God, being a free man and of good report.
W. M. - The tongue of good report has already been heard in his favour; do you, Bro. Inner Guard, vouch that he is properly prepared?
I. G. - (having previously noticed the preparation) I do, Worshipful Master.
W. M. - Then let him be admitted in due form. (I.G. discharges sign of E.A.) Brother Deacons, you will attend to your duties.
(The Deacons go to the door, the Candidate is admitted. The I.G. takes Can.’s right hand in his own left, and applies the Poniard to the naked 1eft breast, asking him if he feels any thing. After reply in the affirmative, he raises the Poniard above his head and steps back to the back of the S.W.’s chair. The Candidate is then led to the left of the S.W. by the J.D.)
W. M. - Mr. A. B., as no person can be made a Freemason unless he is a free man and of mature age, I demand to know if you are free and of the full age of twenty-one years.
CAN. - I am.
W. M. - Thus assured, I will thank you to kneel, while the blessing of Heaven is invoked in aid of our proceedings.
(The Can. kneels, the Deacons stand one on either side, with their wands crossed so as to meet over the head of the Candidate)
W. M. (gives one knock which the Wardens repeat)
To order, Brethren. (all stand with the sign of fidelity)
Chaplain - Vouchsafe Thine aid, Almighty Father and Supreme Ruler of the Universe, to this Convention, and grant that this Candidate for Freemasonry may so dedicate and devote his life to Thy service that he may become a true and faithful Brother among us; indue him with a competence of Thy Divine Wisdom, so that, assisted by the teaching of our Masonic Art, he may be enabled to display the beauties of true godliness, to the honour and glory of thy Holy Name. So Mote It Be. (all discharge sign of fidelity)
W. M. - Brethren, be seated.
W. M. - (Candidate still kneeling) Mr. A. B., in your present circumstances, and in all cases of difficulty or danger, in whom do you put your trust?
CAN. - (prompted by J.D.) In God.
W. M. - Right glad am I to find your faith so well founded; relying on His sure support, you may safely arise and accompany your guide with firm but humble confidence, for where the Name of God is invoked we trust no danger can ensue. (The Candidate is instructed to rise.) (One knock which the Wardens repeat) The Brethren in the north, east, south and west will take notice that Mr. A. B. is about to pass in view before them, to show that he is properly prepared to be made a Freemason.

sections.heading: Presentation, obligation and symbolic light
sections.body:
(The J.D. takes the Can. as before by the right hand, instructs him to start off with the left foot, and walks along the edge of the chequered floor with the Can. on his left and the S.D. walking behind the Can. and leads him round to the centre of the J.W.’s pedestal. Can. is placed facing J.W. and J.D. takes Can.'s right hand to knock once on the extended right arm of the J.W.)
J. W. - Whom have you here?
J. D. - Mr. A. B., a poor Candidate in a state of darkness who has been well and worthily recommended, regularly proposed and approved in open Lodge, and who now comes, of his own free will and accord, properly prepared, humbly soliciting to be admitted to the mysteries and privileges of antient Freemasonry.
J. W. - How does he hope to obtain those privileges ?
J. D. - By the help of God, being a free man and of good report.
J. W. - (J.W. taking the Can.'s right hand) Enter, free.
(The J.D. conducts the Can. to the centre of the S.W.’s pedestal and places Can. facing S.W., and gives one knock on the extended right arm of the S.W., with the right hand of the Can.)
S. W. - Whom have you here?
J. D. - Mr. A. B., a poor Candidate in a state of darkness who has been well and worthily recommended, regularly proposed and approved in open Lodge, and who now comes, of his own free will and accord, properly prepared, humbly soliciting to be admitted to the mysteries and privileges of antient Freemasonry
S. W. - How does he hope to obtain those privileges ?
J. D. - By the help of God, being a free man and of good report.
S. W. - (S.W. taking the Can.'s right hand) Enter, free. (S.W. passes Can.’s right hand to J.D. who conducts Can. to the left of the S.W. and facing the W.M. The S.W. takes the Can.'s right hand in his left hand.)
S. W. (rising with the sign of fidelity )
Worshipful Master, I present to you Mr. A. B., a Candidate properly prepared to be made a Freemason. (S.W. remains standing with sign of fidelity.)
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden I will attend to your presentation; but I will first address certain questions to the Candidate, which I trust he will answer with truth and candour. (W.M. pauses until S.W. passes Can.’s hand to J.D. and is seated ) Mr. A. B., do you seriously declare upon your honour that, unbiased by the improper solicitation of friends against your own inclination, and uninfluenced by mercenary or any other unworthy motives, you offer yourself freely and voluntarily as a Candidate for the mysteries and privileges of antient Freemasonry?
CAN. - I do.
W. M. - Do you likewise declare that you are prompted to solicit those privileges by a favourable opinion preconceived of the Institution, by a general desire for Knowledge, and by a sincere wish to render yourself more extensively serviceable to your fellow-men?
CAN. - I do.
W. M. - Do you further seriously declare upon your honour, that, avoiding fear on the one hand and levity and rashness on the other, you will steadily persevere through the ceremony of your Initiation, and if once admitted among us, you will always act up to and abide by the antient usages and established customs of our Order?
CAN. - I will.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, (W.M. pauses, S.W. rises with sign of fidelity) you will direct the Junior Deacon to instruct the Candidate to advance to the east by the proper steps.
(S.W. discharges sign and sits)
S. W. - Bro. Junior Deacon, (J.D. salutes the S.W. by holding the wand over the left breast) it is the Worshipful Master's command that you instruct the Candidate to advance to the east by the proper steps. (J.D. discharges sign)
(The J. C. conducts the Can. down the North, along the East to a position centre of the W.M.’s pedestal, stops and places Can. facing the W.M. about six feet from the Pedestal.)
J. D. - The method of advancing from west to east in this Degree is by three irregular steps. You will take a short step forward with your left foot, (Can. does accordingly) place your right foot with the heel touching the heel of your left foot to form a square or 90°. (J.D.assists the Can. if necessary) Next, take a slightly longer step forward and place your right foot with the heel touching the heel of your left foot to form a square or 90° (Can. does accordingly) Finally, take a long step forward with your left foot and place your right foot as before to form a square or 90°.
(The Can. is now immediately in front of the Pedestal. S.D. to the left and J.D. to the right of the Can., one pace back.)
W. M. - Mr. A. B., it is my duty to inform you that the Speculative Masonry which we practise is essentially free, and that it requires a perfect freedom of inclination in every Candidate for its Mysteries; it is founded upon the purest principles of piety and virtue; it possesses many great and invaluable privileges, and in order, as far as is possible, to secure those privileges to worthy men alone, vows of fidelity are required; but let me assure you that those vows are in no way incompatible with your moral, your civil, or your religious duties. Are you, then, willing to take a Solemn
Obligation founded upon, and in strict accordance with, the principles which I have stated, to keep inviolate the secrets and mysteries of our Order?
CAN. - I am.
W. M. - Then you will kneel on your left knee, keeping your right foot at right angles with the body, and the body erect ; give me your right hand, which I place on this book, the Volume of Sacred Laws (commonly called the Bible), while with your hand you support the Compasses with one point presented to your naked left breast, and say after me, repeating your several names at length.
(W. M. gives one knock, which is repeated by the Wardens. The W.M. and all the brethren rise, and all place the right hand on the heart. Deacons cross their wands over the Can.’s head.)
W. M. - I, A. B., in the presence of The Great Architect Of The Universe, and of this Worthy and Worshipful Lodge of Antient Free and Accepted Masons, lawfully constituted, and regularly assembled, of my own free will and accord do hereby (W.M. touches Can.’s right hand with his right hand) and hereon (W.M. touches the V.S.L. with his right hand and returns back to sign of fidelity) most solemnly and sincerely swear that I will always hele, conceal, and never wilfully reveal any or either of the secrets or mysteries of, or at all belonging to, Freemasonry, which shall now or may at any future time be communicated to me, to any individual whomsoever, except it be to one who has been properly proposed, and duly elected and has been presented, a Candidate properly prepared to be made a Freemason, and then only in the body of a Lodge Just, Perfect, and Regular. I further solemnly promise that I will not write those secrets, indite, carve, mark, engrave, or otherwise them delineate, or cause or suffer the same to be so done by others, if in my power to prevent it, upon anything movable or immovable, whereby or whereon any letter, character or figure, or the least trace of any letter, character or figure, may become legible or intelligible, so that our Secret Arts and Hidden Mysteries may improperly become known through my unworthiness. These several points I solemnly swear to observe, without evasion, equivocation, or mental reservation of any kind, in the certain knowledge, that on the violation of any of them, I shall be branded as a wilfully perjured individual, void of all moral worth, and totally unfit to be received into this or any other warranted Lodge, or any society of men who prize Truth and Honour above the external advantages of rank and fortune. So help me God, and may He keep me steadfast in this the great and Solemn Obligation of an Entered Apprentice Freemason. (W.M. removes the Compasses from the Can.’s left hand while Can.’s right hand remains on the V.S.L.)
W. M. - As a pledge of your fidelity to this solemn Obligation, I call upon you to seal it upon the Volume of Sacred Laws once with your lips.
(Can. kisses the V.S.L. once. W.M. and all Brethren discharge sign of fidelity.)
W. M. - Having been kept for some time in a state of darkness, what at the present moment is the predominant wish of your heart?
CAN. - (prompted by the J.D.) Light.
W. M. - Let that blessing be restored.
(The W. M. takes his gavel, and simultaneously the Brethren clap their hands loudly. At the same time, the J.D. removes the hoodwink, follow by the cable tow.)
W. M. - Having been restored to the blessing of material light, let me direct your attention to the three Great Emblematical Lights in Freemasonry, namely, (points to V.S.L.) the Volume of Sacred Laws, (points the Square) the Square, and (points the Compasses) the Compasses. The Sacred Writings are to rule and direct our Faith, the Square to regulate our Actions, and the Compasses to keep us within due bounds with all mankind, more particularly with our Brethren in Freemasonry.
(The W. M. takes the Can. by the right hand.)
W. M. - Rise, duly obligated Novice in the First Degree of Freemasonry. (W.M. passes Can.’s right hand to J.D.) Brethren, be seated.
(J.D. conducts Can. along the East, South, West and North to the North-East corner, and places Can. facing South.)
W. M. - Principal officers be upstanding. (W.M., S.W. and J.W. stand up) I am now enabled to point out to you the three Lesser Lights in Freemasonry; they are situated due West, South, and East, and represent the Sun, the Moon, and the Master of the Lodge: the Sun to rule the day, the Moon to govern the night, and the Master to rule and direct the Lodge. (speaks to Wardens) Brother Wardens, be seated. (W.M., and Wardens sit)
By your very decorous behaviour this evening you have escaped two great dangers, namely, those of stabbing and strangulation; for at your entrance into the Lodge, this Poniard (W.M. shows poniard) was presented to your naked left breast so that if you had rashly attempted to rush forward you might have been accessory to your own death by stabbing while the Brother who held it would but have remained firm and have done his duty. That Cable Tow also (shows cable tow) , with a running noose was placed about your neck so that any attempt to retreat might have been equally fatal by strangulation. But there is a third danger which will await you to the latest period of your life, namely, that on any violation of your Obligation, you will be branded as a wilfully perjured individual, void of all moral worth, and totally unfit to be received into this, or any other warranted Lodge, or any society of men who prize Truth and Honour above the external advantages of rank and fortune.
(The W. M. descends from the dais and stands on the south-east side of the Lodge, facing the Can.)

sections.heading: Signs, tokens and examination
sections.body:
W. M. - Now that you have taken upon you the Great and Solemn Obligation of an Entered Apprentice Freemason, I am permitted to inform you that there are several degrees in Freemasonry, with peculiar Secrets restricted to each. These, however, are not communicated indiscriminately, but are conferred upon Candidates according to merit and ability. I will now proceed to intrust you with the Secrets of this Degree, comprising the signs by which Freemasons are known to each other, and are distinguished from the rest of the world. But I will premise for your general information that all Squares and Perpendiculars (when applied to the position of the Body and its Limbs ) are true and proper Signs by which to know a Freemason. You are therefore expected to stand perfectly erect, with your feet in the form of a Square (W.M. shows Can. and he does the same); your body in its erect posture being an emblem of the uprightness of your mind, and your feet in their rectangular position being symbolical of the rectitude of your actions. You will now take a short pace forward with you left foot, bring the right heel into its hollow. That is the First Regular Step in Freemasonry, and it is in this position that the Secrets of this Degree are communicated. They consist of a Sign, a Grip or Token, and a Word. The Sign is given thus - (W.M. demonstrates) You will place your right hand in this position with the thumb extended in the form of a square to the left of the windpipe. The sign is given by drawing the hand smartly across the throat and dropping it to the side. (Can. copies) This is called the Penal Sign, it alludes to the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree and implied that as a man of honour and an Entered Apprentice Freemason you would rather have had your throat cut across, your tongue torn out by the roots and your body buried in the sands of the sea, at least a cable length from high water mark where the tide regularly ebb and flow twice in the course of a natural day, than improperly divulge the Secrets of this degree. The Grip or Token is a distinct pressure of the thumb on the first knuckle of the hand. To this Grip a Word is attached, one highly prized among Freemasons, as a guard to their privileges. Too much caution cannot, therefore, be observed in communicating it. You must never give it at length, but always by, lettering or halving it, except in open Lodge. Being now in open Lodge, I will, for your instruction, give the Word in full. It is BOAZ. (W.M. spells it) As you will shortly be called upon for this Grip and Word, the Junior Deacon will now give the answers which you will then have to repeat for yourself.
W. M. - What is this?
J. D. - The Grip or Token of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
W. M. - What does this Grip demand?
J. D. - A Word.
W. M. - Give me that Word.
J. D. - At my initiation I was taught to be cautious; I will letter or halve it with you.
W. M. - I greatly commend your caution; letter it, and I will begin. (W.M. begins with letter B follow by Can. with letter O, etc.) Halve it, and you will begin. (Can. begins with BO follow by W.M. with AZ) This Word is derived from the left hand pillar, at the porchway or entrance of King Solomon Temple. It is so named after Boaz, the great grandfather of David, a Prince and Ruler in Israel, and the import of the word is in Strength. The Junior Deacon will now conduct you to the Wardens for trial and probation. (W.M. returns to his seat)
I. P.M. (steps down the dais and faces Can.)
You will shortly be called upon to salute the Worshipful Master in passing as an Entered Apprentice. I will demonstrate the manner of saluting and you will copy my example when called upon to do so. (I.P.M. demonstrates salute and then returns to his seat)
J. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master in passing as an Entered Apprentice. (Can. salutes in passing, J.D. salutes with wand)
16
(The J.D. leads the Can. to the centre of the J.W.’s pedestal. J.D. positions himself on the right of the pedestal facing East, passes his wand to the S.D. and salute the J.W. with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice.)
J. D. - Bro. Junior Warden, I present to you Bro. A. B. on his Initiation. (J.D. discharges sign)
J. W. - Bro. A. B., you will now advance to me as an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
(The J.D. instructs the Can. to advance with the First Regular Step and J.W. replies by rising and advancing with the first regular step.)
J. W. - What is that?
CAN. - (prompted by J.D.) The First Regular Step in Freemasonry.
J. W. - Do you bring anything else?
CAN. - I do. (J.D. gives the Penal Sign and instructs the Can. to copy his example.)
J. W. - What is that?
CAN. - (prompted by the J.D.) The Penal Sign of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
J. W. - To what does it allude?
CAN. - (prompted by the J.D.) To the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in my Obligation.
J. W. - What does it imply?
CAN. - That as a man of honour and an Entered Apprentice Freemason, I would rather have my throat cut across (J.D.
demonstrates and instructs the Can. to make the cutting motion) than improperly reveal the secrets of this degree. (J.W. replies with cutting motion)
J. W. - Have you anything further to communicate?
CAN. - I have.
(The J.D. raises Can.’s right hand to give the Grip to J.W. and maintains it.)
J. W. - What is this?
CAN. - The Grip or Token of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
J. W. - What does this Grip demand?
CAN. - A Word.
J. W. - Give me that Word.
CAN. - At my initiation I was taught to be cautious; I will letter or halve it with you.
J. W. - I greatly commend your caution. I will letter it, and I will begin. (J.W. begins with letter B follow by Can. with letter O, etc.) Halve it, and you will begin. (Can. begins with BO follow by J.W. with AZ) Pass Boaz. (J.W. passes Can.’s right hand to J.D. and S.D. returns wand to J.D.)
(The J.D. leads the Can. to the centre of the S.W.’s pedestal. J.D. positions himself on the right of the pedestal facing South, passes his wand to the S.D. and salute the S.W. with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice.)
J. D. - Bro. Senior Warden, I present to you Bro. A. B. on his Initiation. (J.D. discharges sign)
S. W. - Bro. A. B., you will now advance to me as an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
(The J.D. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to advance with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice and S.W. rises to reply with step and sign of an E.A.)
S. W. - Have you anything further to communicate?
CAN. - I have. (The J.D. raises Can.’s right hand to give the Grip to S.W. and maintains it.)
S. W. - What is this?
CAN. - (prompted by the J.D.) The Grip or Token of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
S. W. - What does this Grip demand?
CAN. - A Word.
S. W. - Give me that Word.
CAN. - At my initiation I was taught to be cautious; I will letter or halve it with you.
S. W. - I greatly commend your caution. I will letter it, and I will begin. (S.W. begins with letter B follow by Can. with letter O, etc.) Halve it, and you will begin. (Can. begins with BO follow by J.W. with AZ) Pass Boaz. (J.W. passes Can.’s right hand to J.D.
S. W. - Whence is this Word derived ?
CAN. - From the left hand pillar at the porchway or entrance of King Solomon Temple.
S. W - After whom is it named?
CAN. - After Boaz, the great grandfather of David, a Prince and Ruler in Israel.
S. W. - What is the import of the Word ?
CAN. - In Strength.
S. W. - Pass Boaz in strength.
(S.W. passes Can.’s right hand to J.D. and S.D. returns wand to J.D. who then conducts Can. to the left of the S.W. who takes Can.’s right hand in his own left.)
S. W. - (rises with sign of E.A.) Worshipful Master, I present to you Bro. A. B. on his Initiation, for some further mark of your favour. (S.W. remains standing and maintains sign)

summary: Explore the apron, charitable lesson, working tools and moral charge.

sections.heading: Investiture and the north-east corner
sections.body:
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, I delegate to Bro. M.M. the authority to invest our Brother with the distinguishing Badge of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
(S.W. discharges sign and sits. J.D. brings Can. to a few paces down the North-West corner facing South. The D. of C. gets the E.A. apron ready. Brother M.M. goes in front of Can. )
M. M. (salutes W.M. and then faces Can.)
Bro. A. B., by the Worshipful Master's command, I invest you with the distinguishing Badge of an Entered Apprentice Freemason. It is more antient than the Golden Fleece or the Roman Eagle, more honourable than the Garter, or any other Order in existence, being the Badge of Innocence and the Bond of Friendship; and I strongly exhort you always to wear and to consider it in that character. You will observe that this Apron is made from the skin of a Lamb, and, as the Lamb has been from time immemorial the universally acknowledged emblem of Purity and Innocence, you will be thereby reminded of the purity of life and actions which should always distinguish a Freemason, and which is most essential to your gaining admission to that Grand Lodge above, where the blessed ever rest in eternal peace. We trust that you may live many years to wear that Badge, with pleasure to yourself, with usefulness to the Craft, and with honour to the Lodge in which you have been initiated; and let me further exhort you never to disgrace that Badge, for be assured that it will never disgrace you. I will add that you are never to put on that Badge and to enter a Lodge where there is a Brother against whom you may entertain any feelings of animosity. In such a case, it is expected that you will invite him to withdraw, in order that you may settle your differences amicably; which having been happily effected, you may then clothe yourselves and enter the Lodge, and work together with the love and harmony which should always characterise Freemasons. But if, unfortunately, your differences should be of such a nature as not to be so easily adjusted, it were better that one or both of you should retire, rather than that the harmony of the Lodge should be interrupted by your presence. (Brother M.M. salutes W.M. and returns to his seat)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Deacon, you will now place our newly-initiated Brother in the North-East corner of the Lodge.
(J.D. brings Can. to North-East corner of the Lodge and places him facing South. The Brother who is giving the N.E. corner address stands in the S.E. corner of the Lodge.)
M. M. (salutes W.M. and then faces Can.)
It is customary at the erection of all stately and superb edifices, whether intended for sacred or secular uses, to lay the ‘ chief cornerstone ' in the north-east corner of the building; you being newly initiated into Freemasonry, are placed in the north-east corner of the Lodge, figuratively to represent that stone; and upon the foundation which we have this day laid, we trust you may hereafter raise a superstructure, perfect in all its parts, and honourable to the Builder.
You now stand to all external appearance a just and upright man and Freemason; and I earnestly exhort you always to act up to that character. Indeed, I shall immediately proceed to put your principles in some measure to the test, by calling upon you to exercise that virtue which may justly be denominated the distinguishing characteristic of a Freemason's heart, namely, Charity. I trust I need not here dilate upon its excellences; doubtless it has often been felt and practised by you; it will be sufficient for me to say that it has the approbation of Heaven and of Earth: and, like its sister, Mercy, it bestows a double blessing:
'It blesseth him that gives and him that takes.'
In a Fraternity so widely extended as Freemasonry is, having its branches spread over the whole habitable globe, it cannot be denied that we have many Brethren of rank and opulence among us; neither, on the other hand, can it be concealed that among the thousands who range under its banners, there are many who, perhaps from circumstances of unforeseen misfortune or calamity, are reduced to the lowest state of poverty and distress. In their behalf it is our usual custom to awaken the sympathies of every newly-initiated Brother, by making such a claim upon his Charity as his position and circum- stances in life may fairly warrant; anything therefore that you may feel disposed to give towards the relief of your distressed Brethren you may deposit with the Junior Deacon; and I assure you it will be thankfully received and faithfully applied.
(The J.D. passes his wand to the S.D., takes the salver from the Secretary’s table and holds it to the Can.)
J. D. - Have you anything to give?
CAN. - (prompted by S.D.) I have not.
J. D. - Were you not divested of money and metals of value, or else you would have given freely?
CAN. - (prompted by S.D.) Yes.
J. D. (with sign of E.A. and holding the sign)
Worshipful Master, the Can. was divested of all money and metals of value or else he would have given freely.
(J.D. discharges sign and returns salver to the Secretary’s table and retrieves his wand from the S.D.)
M. M. - I congratulate you upon the kindly and generous sentiments by which you are actuated, as well as upon the inability which at present precludes you from gratifying them. Believe me, this trial was not made in order to sport with your feelings; far from us be any such intention. It was made for three especial reasons: firstly, to put your principles in some measure to the test; secondly, to evince to the Brethren that you had neither money nor metals of value about you, for, if you had, the Ceremony thus far must have been repeated; and thirdly, as a warning to your own heart, that should you at any future time meet a distressed Brother who may claim your assistance, and whom upon inquiry you may find to be deserving of assistance - not otherwise you would think upon the peculiar occasion when you were admitted into Freemasonry, poor and penniless, and would cheerfully embrace the opportunity of practising on his behalf the virtue of Charity, which in your present impecunious condition you are prevented from doing.
(Brother M.M. salutes W.M. and returns to his seat)

sections.heading: Working tools, authority and retirement
sections.body:
J. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master in passing as an Entered Apprentice.
(J.D. conducts the Can. past the W.M.’s pedestal and Can. salutes on passing the W.M., J.D. salutes with wand and leads Can. down the South and West without saluting the Wardens and stops in front of the Secretary’s table, and then places the Can. facing the J.W.)
J. W. (rises and salutes the W.M. as an E.A.)
Bro. A. B., I will now explain the Working Tools of an Entered Apprentice Freemason. They are the Twenty-four Inch Gauge, the Common Gavel and the Chisel. (The implement is shown when mentioned.)
The Twenty-four Inch Gauge is the implement with which we measure our work.
The Common Gavel is to knock off all superfluous knobs and excrescences.
And the Chisel is to further smooth and prepare the Stone, for the hands of the more expert Craftsman.
Those are the uses of these implements in operative Masonry; but we, not professing to be Operative, but Free and Accepted or Speculative Masons, apply these Tools to our Morals. In this sense, the Twenty-four Inch Gauge represents to us the twenty-four hours of the day, part to be spent in prayer to Almighty God, part in labour and refreshment, and part to serve a friend or Brother in his time of need, as far as may fairly be done without detriment to ourselves or our connections.
The common Gavel represents to us the force of Conscience, which should keep down all vain and unbecoming thoughts which may obtrude themselves during the before-named periods of the day, so that all our thoughts, words, and actions may appear before the Throne of Grace, pure and unpolluted.
The Chisel points out to us the advantages of a liberal and enlightened Education, by which means alone we are rendered fit members of regularly organised Society.
(J.W. salutes the W.M. as an E.A. and sits. J.D. conducts Can. to centre of the Lodge under the G. Bro. Secretary rises and walks onto the chequered floor of the Lodge, salutes the W.M. as an E.A.)
Bro. SEC. - As you have been called upon for certain Fees for your Initiation, it is right that I should inform you by what authority we act. This (points to Charter) is our Charter or Warrant of Constitution from the Grand Lodge of England, under which we are authorised to hold meetings, to initiate Candidates, and to demand Fees for their initiation. This is open for your inspection now or at any future time. This (holds up Book) is the Book of Constitutions, and these (holds up Bye-laws) are our Bye-laws, both of which I recommend to your serious attention; as by the one you will be taught the duties you owe to the Craft in general, and by the other
those that are due to this Lodge in particular. (Bro. Secretary salutes W.M. as an E.A. and returns to his seat)
(J.D. conducts Can. directly up to the East to the W.M.’s pedestal.)
W. M. - You may now retire, in order to restore yourself to your formal comfort and on your return into the Lodge your attention will be directed to a Charge, founded upon the excellence of our Institution and the qualifications of its members.
(J.D. places the Can. one pace back from the W.M.’s pedestal.)
J. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice Freemason. (Can. salutes)
(J.D. conducts Can. to the North-West corner of the Lodge and places Can. on his left, both facing the W.M.) W. M. (while J.D. with Can. passes the J.W.)
Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. rises with step and sign of E.A.) you will pass out our Candidate.
(J.W. discharges sign and sits)
J. D. - It is customary on entering or leaving the Lodge to salute the W.M. with the step and sign of the degree in which the Lodge is working. As we are in the Entered Apprentice degree, you will salute the W.M. with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice Freemason by copying me.
(J.D. hands wand to S.D. and salutes the W.M. with the step and sign of an E.A., ensuring that the Can. does at the same time.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of E.A.) you will pass out our Candidate.
(I.G. discharges sign, goes to the door and opens it. Meanwhile, J.D. retrieves his wand, turns anti-clockwise and leads Can. to the door where the Tyler waits to receive Can. I.G. closes the door. J.D. and S.D. return to the North-West corner and both march smartly up the North. S.D. stands at his position at the N.E. corner. J.D. salutes with his wand in passing the W.M. along the East, up the South without saluting the J.W. and takes his position in the S.W. corner of the Lodge. Both Deacons place their wands in the stands and sit down in unison.)

sections.heading: The charge to the new member
sections.body:
THE CHARGE
(Can., having changed into his formal comfort, waits outside the door of the Lodge. Tyler gives three knocks on the door.)
I. G. (rises with step and sign of E.A., and holds the sign)
Bro. Junior Warden, there is a report. (I.G. discharges sign.)
J. W. (rises with step and sign of E.A. and holding the sign.)
Worshipful Master, there is a report.
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, you will see who seeks admission. Should it be the return of our newly initiated Brother, admit him.
(J.W. discharges the sign and sits.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of E.A. and holding the sign.) you will see who seeks admission. Should it be the return of our newly initiated Brother, admit him.
(I.G. discharges the sign, goes to the door, opens it and admits the Can. who waits for the Deacons to come and conduct him. J.D. conducts Can. to the North-West corner of the Lodge.)
J. W. - You will salute the Worshipful Master with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice.
(Can. salutes the W.M. as instructed. J.D. conducts Can. up the North side to the mid-point near the Secretary’s table, cuts in to the centre of the chequered floor, stops under the G and places Can. facing the W.M.)
(P.M. walks onto the chequered floor, salutes the W.M. with the step and sign of an E.A. and faces the Can.)
P. M. - Bro. Deacons, be seated. (P.M. waits for Deacons to be seated) Now that you have passed through the Ceremony of your Initiation, allow me (on behalf of the Worshipful Master, and the Brethren of this Lodge), to congratulate you on having become a member of our Antient and Honourable Fraternity.
Antient it undoubtedly is, having subsisted from time immemorial, and Honourable it must be acknowledged to be, because by a natural tendency it conduces to render all those honourable who are strictly obedient to its precepts. Indeed, no Institution can boast a more solid foundation than that upon which Freemasonry rests, namely, the practice of every moral and social virtue; and to so high an eminence has its credit been advanced that monarchs in every age have been promoters of the art, have not thought it derogatory to their dignity to exchange the sceptre for the gavel, have patronised our mysteries, and have joined in our assemblies.
As a Freemason, I would first recommend to your serious study the volume of the Sacred Law, charging you to consider it as the unerring standard of truth and justice, and to regulate your actions by the Divine precepts which it contains; therein you will be taught the important duties you owe to God, to your neighbour and to yourself.
To God, by never mentioning His name but with that awe and reverence which are due from the creature to his Creator, by rendering to Him the tribute of praise and thanksgiving, for His manifold and great mercies and blessings; by imploring His aid upon all your lawful undertakings, and by looking up to Him in every emergency for comfort and support.
To your neighbour, by acting with him upon the Square, by rendering to him every kind office which justice or mercy may require, by soothing his afflictions, by relieving his necessities, and by doing unto him in all things as in similar cases you would wish that he should do unto you.
And to yourself, by such a prudent and well-regulated course of discipline, as may best conduce to the preservation of your corporeal and mental faculties in their fullest energy, thereby enabling you to employ those talents wherewith God has blessed you, as well to His glory as to the welfare of your fellow-creatures.
As a Citizen of the World, I have next to enjoin you to be exemplary in the discharge of your Civil Duties, by never proposing or at all countenancing any act which may have a tendency to subvert the peace and good order of Society; by rendering due obedience to the laws of this, or of any other Kingdom or State, which may for a time, or in permanence, become the place of your residence or may afford you its protection; and above all by an unwavering allegiance to the Sovereign of your Native Land, ever remembering that nature has implanted in the breast of man a sacred, and it should be an indissoluble, attachment to the country from which he derives his birth and his infant nurture. As an Individual, I would further recommend to you the practice of every Domestic as well as public Virtue : let Temperance chasten you, Fortitude support you, Prudence direct you, and Justice be the guide of all your actions; being at all times especially careful to maintain in unsullied brightness that truly Masonic Jewel which has been already amply illustrated, namely, Charity.
Still, as a Freemason, there are other excellences of character to which your attention may be peculiarly and forcibly directed. Among the foremost of these are Secrecy, Fidelity, and Obedience. The Secrecy required of you is an inviolable adherence to the O... which you have entered into, never improperly to divulge any of those Masonic Secrets which have now been, or may hereafter be, communicated to you, and carefully to avoid all occasions which may inadvertently lead you to betray them.
Your Fidelity must be exemplified by a close conformity to the Constitutions of the Fraternity, by adhering to the Antient Landmarks of the Order, by never attempting to extort or to otherwise improperly obtain the Secrets of a Superior Degree, and by refraining from recommending anyone to participation in the
Secrets and Privileges of Freemasonry, unless from an intimate personal knowledge of --- or after full inquiry into his character you shall have good grounds for believing that by a regular and well ordered life, guided in all things in accordance with the Tenets and Principles of the Order, he will ultimately reflect honour upon the Lodge.
Your Obedience must be proved by a strict observance of our Laws and Regulations, by prompt attention to all Signs and Summonses, by modest and correct demeanour in the Lodge, by abstaining, while there, from every topic of religious or political discussion, by a ready acquiescence in all Votes and Resolutions duly passed by a majority of the Brethren, and by a perfect submission to the will of the Master and the Wardens of the Lodge, when acting in the discharge of the duties of their respective offices.
And as a last general recommendation, let me exhort you to dedicate yourself to such pursuits as may enable you to become at once respectable in life, useful to mankind, and an honour to the Fraternity of which you have this day been admitted a member. That you will more especially cultivate such of the Liberal Arts and Sciences as may lie within the compass of your attainment; and that without neglecting the ordinary duties of your station in life, you will feel yourself called upon to make a daily advancement in Masonic Knowledge.
From the exemplary manner in which you have conducted yourself during the Ceremony of your Initiation, and from the very commendable attention you have given to this Charge, we are led to hope that you will duly appreciate the value of Freemasonry, and that there may be indelibly imprinted upon your heart the sacred principles of Truth, of Honour, and of Virtue. So Mote It Be.
(P.M. salutes the W.M. with step and sign of E.A. and returns to his seat. Both Deacons resume their positions on either side of the Can. and J.D. brings Can. directly up to the W.M.’s pedestal.)
W. M. - Let me be the first to congratulate you on being initiated in Freemasonry. (hand shake with Can.) Here is a set of Questions and Answers (gives Q & A to Can.) with a number of blanks which your proposer or seconder or any Brother can fill in for you. You are required to learn those Questions and Answers before you can be passed to the Second Degree. You may now take your seat in the North-East of the Lodge.
(J.D. places Can. one pace back from the W.M.’s pedestal)
J. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master with the step and sign of an Entered Apprentice. (Can. does as instructed)
(J.D. conducts the Can. past the J.W., S.W., and the Secretary without saluting in passing and seats him in the North-East of the Lodge. S.D. stands at his position in the N.E., J.D salutes with his wand in passing the W.M., past the J.W. and takes his position in the S.W. Both Deacons place their wands in the stands and sit in unison.

title: Entered Apprentice: closing the lodge
summary: Follow the closing dialogue and ceremonial directions in full.

sections.heading: The first-degree closing sequence
sections.body:
The Ceremony of Closing the Lodge.
(The W.M. rises and gives one knock which is answered by the S.W. and the J.W.)
W. M. - Brethren, assist me to close the Lodge. (All rise.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) what is the constant care of every Freemason?
J. W. - To prove the Lodge close tyled.
W. M. - You will direct that duty to be done. (J.W. discharges the sign of E.A.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) you will prove the Lodge close tyled.
(The I.G. discharges sign of E.A. and gives the 3 knocks, which are answered by the Tyler.)
I. G. - (with step and sign of E.A.) Bro. Junior Warden, the Lodge is close tyled
. J. W. - (rises with step and sign of E.A.) Worshipful Master, the Lodge is close tyled.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, (S.W. responds with and holds the sign of E.A.) what is our next care ?
S. W. - To see that the Brethren appear to order as Freemasons. (S.W. discharges the sign of E.A.)
W. M. - Brethren, to order as Freemasons. (All stand to order as E.A.)
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, your constant place in the Lodge?
S. W. - In the West.
W. M. - Why are you so placed?
S. W. - As the sun sets in the West to close the day, so the Senior Warden is placed in the West to close the Lodge by the Worshipful Master's command, after having seen that every Brother has had his due.
Chaplain - Brethren, before the Lodge is closed, let us with all reverence and humility express our gratitude to The Great Architect Of The Universe for the favours which we have received, and may He continue to preserve our Order by adorning its members with every moral and social virtue. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, the labours of the day being ended, you have my command to close the Lodge.
(W.M. keeps up the sign ; gives one knock with the left hand.)
S. W. - Brethren, by command of the Worshipful Master, I close the Lodge.
(At the word ' close,' all drop the sign in unison. The S.W. gives one knock. The J.D. goes to the Secretary’s table and the S.D. goes to the J.W.’s pedestal. I.P.M. goes to the centre of the Lodge under the ‘G’. Deacons cross their wands with a click to signal the I.P.M. to walk to the W.M.’s pedestal escorted by the Deacons with wands crossed. I.P.M. kneel on his left knee and close the V.S.L. and place the Square and Compasses on it. I.P.M. gives a court bow to the W.M. and returns to his seat. Both Deacons give court bow and return to their respective positions and place their wands in the stands. J.D. closes the first degree tracing board and S.D. puts out the candle on W.M.’s pedestal. S.W. and J.W. put out their candles and S.W. lowers his column to a horizontal position.)
J. W. - And it is closed accordingly until the fourth Wednesday in the ensuing month, except in case of emergency, of which due notice will be given.
(J.W. gives one knock, followed by the I.G. and the Tyler. J.W. raises his column to an upright position.)
I. P. M. (steps down to the floor of the Lodge in front of the W.M.’s pedestal and places his right hand on the closed V.S.L.)
Brethren, nothing now remains but, according to ancient custom, that each Brother lock up the secrets of the Lodge in the safe and sacred repository, the heart, uniting in the act of Fidelity, Fidelity, Fidelity (all give sign of fidelity 3 times), and may God be with us all. So Mote It Be.
(All Brethren remain standing while the D. of C. leads the J.D. from his position, follow by the S.D. taking his position on the J.D.’s left, then the J.W. taking his position behind the Deacons, then the S.W. taking his position on the J.W.’s left and then the W.M. taking his position behind the Deacons and in front of the Wardens. Deacons cross the wands at the door for the W.M. and Wardens to pass under.

sources.title: UGLE: Freemasonry questions and the three degrees

title: Fellow Craft: preparation and first-degree questions
summary: Read the preparatory opening, first-degree examination and transition.

sections.heading: Opening in the first degree
sections.body:
2nd Degree
The Ceremony of Opening the Lodge in the First Degree.
(The Brethren having assembled in the Lodge, the W.M., Wardens and Deacons form up in processional order outside. The Deacons with their wands, the S.D. on the left, take their positions in the front. The W.M. takes his place behind the Deacons and the Wardens behind the W.M. with the J.W. on the left. The Asst. D. of C. gives one knock on the door.)
A. D. of C. - Brethren, be upstanding to receive the Worshipful Master and his officers.
(The Asst. D. of C. leads in the W.M. and his officers. The Deacons cross the wands for the W.M. to take his position in the East, the J.W. in the South and the S.W. in the West. The S.D. and the J.D. are then placed in their positions. All remain standing. The W.M. gives one knock with his gavel, which the Wardens repeat.)
W. M. (addressing visitors, if any)
Centenary Lodge welcome our visitors and we hope that you will stay for our festive board.
W. M. - Brethren, assist me to open the Lodge.
W. M. (addressing the J.W. by name and without sign)
Bro. A., what is the first care of every Freemason?
J. W (with sign of fidelity)
To see that the Lodge is properly tyled.
W. M. - You will direct that duty to be done.
J. W. (to I.G., by name and without sign)
Bro. B., you will see that the Lodge is properly tyled.
(The I.G. opens the door, and sees that the Tyler is at his post.)
I. G. (to J.W., by name and with sign of fidelity) - Bro. A., the Lodge is properly tyled.
J. W. (to W.M., by name and with sign of fidelity)
W. Bro. C., the Lodge is properly tyled.
W. M. (to S.W., by name and without sign)
Bro. D., what is our next care?
S. W. (with sign of fidelity)
To see that none but Freemasons are present.
W. M. (to J.W., by name and without sign)
Bro. A., are you confident that none but Freemasons are present?
J. W. (with sign of fidelity) - I am, W. Bro. C.
W. M. - Brethren, to order as Freemasons.
(All stand to order as Entered Apprentices; and henceforward the Officers are called by the names of their respective offices.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, how many Principal Officers are there in a Lodge?
J. W. - Three, namely, the Worshipful Master and the Senior and Junior Wardens.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, how many Assistant Officers are there? S. W. - Three, besides the Outer Guard or Tyler - namely, the Senior and Junior Deacons and the Inner Guard.
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, the situation of the Outer Guard or Tyler?
J. W. - Outside the door of the Lodge.
W. M. (to J.W.) - What is his duty?
J. W. - Being armed with a drawn sword, his duty is to keep off all cowans, and intruders, and to see that the Candidates for each Degree are properly prepared.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, the situation of the Inner Guard?
S. W. - Within the entrance of the Lodge.
W. M. - Bro. Inner Guard, what is your duty?
I. G. - To admit Freemasons on proof, to receive Candidates in due form, and to obey the commands of the Junior Warden.
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, the situation of the Junior Deacon?
J. W. - At the right hand of the Senior Warden.
W. M. - Bro. Junior Deacon, what is your duty ?
J. D. - To carry all messages and communications of the Worshipful Master from the Senior to the Junior Warden, and to see them punctually obeyed.
W. M. - (to S.W.) The situation of the Senior Deacon?
S. W. - At the right hand of, and near to, the Worshipful Master.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Deacon, what is your duty ?
S. D. - To bear all messages and commands from the Worshipful Master to the Senior Warden, and to await the return of the Junior Deacon.
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, your constant place in the Lodge?
J. W. - In the South.
W. M. - Why are you so placed?
J. W. - To mark the sun at its meridian, and to call the Brethren from labour to refreshment, and from refreshment to labour, so that profit and pleasure may be the result.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, your constant place in the Lodge?
S. W. - In the West.
W. M. - Why are you so placed?
S. W. - To mark the setting sun and to close the Lodge at the Worshipful Master's command.
W. M. (to I.P.M.)
Worthy and Worshipful Past Master, what is the situation of the Worshipful Master?
I. P. M. - In the East.
W. M. - Why is he so placed?
I. P. M. - To represent the rising sun; for as the sun rises in the East to open and enlighten the day, so the Worshipful Master is placed in the East to open his Lodge, and to employ and instruct the Brethren in Freemasonry.
Chaplain - Brethren, the Lodge being thus duly formed, before the Worshipful Master declares it open, let us invoke a blessing from The Great Architect Of The Universe upon all our undertakings; may our labours thus begun in order be conducted in peace and closed in harmony. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Brethren, I declare the Lodge duly opened for the purpose of Freemasonry in the First Degree.
(W.M. gives three knocks with his gavel, which the Wardens repeat. The J.D. goes to the Secretary’s table and the S.D. goes to the J.W.’s pedestal. I.P.M. goes to the centre of the Lodge under the ‘G’. Deacons cross their wands with a click to signal the I.P.M. to walk to the W.M.’s pedestal escorted by the Deacons with wands crossed. I.P.M. kneel on his left knee and open the V.S.L. and arrange the Square and Compasses. I.P.M. salutes the W.M. as an Entered Apprentice and return to his seat. Deacons salute the W.M. with their wands and return to their respective positions and place their wands in the stands. J.D. opens the first degree tracing board and S.D. lights candle on W.M.’s pedestal. S.W. and J.W. light their own candles. The S.W.’s column is places upright and the J.W.’s column is placed horizontal. The I.G. switches on the W.M.’s light and the blue dome light.)
W. M. - Brethren, be seated.

sections.heading: Proficiency questions and explanations
sections.body:
The Ceremony of Passing to the Second Degree (in the First Degree)
(The Junior Deacon should be ready to prompt all answers throughout the Questions and Answers.)
W. M. - (addressing the Lodge) Brethren, Bro. A. B. is this day a Candidate to be passed to the Second Degree; but it is necessary that he should first give proof of his proficiency in the First Degree. I will therefore now ask him the usual questions.
Brother Deacons, you will present the Candidate.
(The J.D. walks to the N.E., takes the Can. and conducts him to the Centre of the Lodge underneath the ‘G’, followed by the S.D. The J.D. stands on the right and S.D. on the left one pace behind the Can.)
W. M. - Where were you first prepared to be made a Freemason?
CAN. - In my heart.
W. M. - Where next?
CAN. - In a convenient room adjoining the Lodge.
W. M. - Describe the mode of your preparation.
CAN. - I was divested of all money and metals of value; I had my right arm, my left breast and left knee made bare and my right heel slip shod with a cable tow about my neck. W. M. - Where were you made a Freemason?
CAN. - In the body of a Lodge, just, perfect and regular.
W. M. - And when?
CAN. - When the sun was at its meridian.
W. M. - Freemasons' Lodges in this country being usually held in the evening, how do you account for this paradox?
CAN. - The sun being the centre of our system, and the earth constantly revolving around it on its own axis, it follows as a first consequence that the sun must always be at its meridian at some part of the earth's surface; and Freemasonry being universally spread over the whole habitable globe, it follows as a second consequence that the sun must always be at its meridian with respect to Freemasonry.
W. M. - What is Freemasonry?
CAN. - A peculiar system of Morality, veiled in allegory, and illustrated by symbols.
W. M. - Name the three Grand Principles upon which it is founded.
CAN. - Brotherly Love, Relief, and Truth.
W. M. - Who are fit and proper persons to be made Freemasons?
CAN. - Just, upright, and free men, of mature age, sound judgement, and strict morals.
W. M. - How do you know yourself to be a Freemason?
CAN. - By the regularity of my Initiation, by repeated trials and probations, and by a willingness at all times to undergo an examination when properly called upon.
W. M. - How would you demonstrate the proof of your being a Freemason to others?
CAN. - By signs, tokens, and the perfect points of my entrance.
W. M. - Those are the usual questions. Has any Brother any other questions he would like to put, to the Candidate?
M. M. - Worshipful Master, can the Candidate explain what makes a Lodge Just, Perfect and Regular and also what are the Perfect Points of his Entrance?
CAN. - I cannot.
W. M. - Bro. M.M., will you please explain them to the Candidate.
M. M. - A Lodge is Just because of the Volume of the Sacred Law, open on the Master's pedestal. It is Perfect because there are seven or more regularly made Freemasons present. It is Regular because of the presence of the Charter or Warrant from the United Grand Lodge of England. The Perfect Points of your Entrance into Freemasonry are indicated by the letters O, A and O. O, on your own free will and accord. A, at the door of the Lodge. O, on the point of a sharp instrument presented to your naked left breast.
M. M. - Worshipful Master, can the Candidate explain the reasons for his preparation before Initiation ?
CAN. - I cannot. W. M. - Bro. M.M., please explain the reasons to the Candidate.
M. M. - I will now explain the reasons for your preparation which at first sight, to your untaught mind, must have appeared somewhat strange; but every part of which has a deep symbolic import and is meant to convey an instructive and useful lesson. Preparation is of two kinds; internal and external. Internally you were prepared in your heart by a favourable impression preconceived of the Institution, a general desire for knowledge and a sincere wish founded on worthy motives to be ranked among its members, thereby enabling you to render yourself more extensively serviceable to your fellow creatures.
Externally you were prepared in a convenient room adjoining the Lodge by having certain portions of your apparel arranged in a peculiar manner to prepare you for the ceremony of your initiation. You were hoodwinked or blindfolded. This was symbolic of your being in a state of darkness respecting the secrets of Freemasonry and to teach you to keep all others in a similar state of darkness until brought to the light; in the same regular manner as you yourself have been. Also that the mind must be made to conceive before the eye call be permitted to discover. A cable tow was placed about your neck, first as a means of restraint, should such have been necessary, and symbolic of your being in a state of bondage, the bondage of ignorance. Your left breast was made bare in token of your fidelity, and to prove that you were not an imposter as to sex, for our rules forbid the admission of females into the order; also that you might be received on the point of a sharp instrument presented thereto and instructed in the usual lessons of fidelity. Your right arm was made bare in token of your sincerity and to prove that you had no weapon of offence or defence about you, for the principles of our order forbid the use of one and that, therefore, automatically renders the use of the other unnecessary. Your left knee was made bare in token of your humility. On it you knelt and in the presence of The Great Architect Of The Universe entered into a solemn obligation never improperly to disclose any of the secrets entrusted to you. You were divested of all money and metals of value. This was to impress upon you that in a Freemasons Lodge, a man is not esteemed on account of his worldly possessions, for therein all men are equal, meeting on the level and parting on the square. It has also reference to the fact that at the building of King Solomon's Temple, it is written "there was no sound of a metal tool heard throughout the building, for the stones were prepared in the quarries, the timbers in the forests, and placed in position with wooden mauls. Your right heel was slipshod. This was in allusion to an ancient custom at the ratification of a bargain or contract such as we find recorded in the 4th Chapter of Ruth, the 7th verse. Now this was the manner in former times in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour and this was a testimony in Israel.

sections.heading: Preparation for passing
sections.body:
W. M. - Do you seriously pledge me your word of honour as a man, and your fidelity as a Freemason, that you will steadily persevere through the ceremony of being passed to the Second Degree?
CAN. - I do.
W. M. - Do you pledge yourself under the penalty of your former obligations that you will conceal that which I am now about to impart to you with the same strict caution as the other secrets in Freemasonry?
CAN. - I do.
W. M. - Then I will entrust you with a test of merit, which consists of a Pass Grip and a Pass Word, leading from the First to the Second Degree.
W. M. - Before I do, I request all Entered Apprentices to retire under the direction of Bro. Asst. Director of Ceremonies. (E.A. is instructed to salute the W.M. in passing as an E.A.)
W. M. - (while E.A. passes the J.W.) Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. rises with step and sign of E.A.) you will pass out our Entered Apprentice.
(J.W. discharges sign of E.A. and sits. E.A. is conducted to the N.W. corner of the Lodge and placed facing East)
A. D. C. - You will salute the Worshipful Master as an Entered Apprentice, taking your time from me.
(A.D.C. salutes the W.M. with step and sign of an E.A. and ensuring that the E.A. does so at the same time.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of E.A.) you will pass out our Entered Apprentice.
(I.G. discharges sign and goes to open the door. The E.A. is turned anti-clockwise and conducted to the door where the Tyler receives him.)
(Can. is conducted to the N.E. of the Lodge and placed facing South. W.M. comes down from the dais and stands in front of the Can. and facing North.)
W. M. - The Pass Grip is given by a distinct pressure between the first and second knuckle joint of the right hand (W.M. demonstrates). The Pass Word is S......... This is a Hebrew word, signifying ‘an Ear of Corn’, or ‘a Flowing Stream’. It is depicted in a Fellow-Crafts' Lodge by an Ear of Corn near a Stream of Water, the import of which symbol is P....y. This Pass Grip and Pass Word you will be required to communicate to the Inner Guard on your return to the Lodge. You will now retire, in order to be prepared for the Second Ceremony. Pass, S......... – P....y.
(W.M. passes Candidate’s hand to J.D. and returns to his seat.)
J. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master in passing as an Entered Apprentice. (J.D. conducts the Can. past the W.M., South, West to the N.W. corner, places Can. on his left, both facing East.)
W. M. - (while J.D. with Can. passes the J.W.) Bro. J.W., (J.W. rises with step and sign of E.A.) you will pass out our Candidate.
(J.W. discharges sign and sits)
J. D. - You will salute the Worshipful Master as an Entered Apprentice taking your time from me.
(J.W. hands wand to S.D. and salutes the W.M. with step and sign of an E.A., ensuring that the Can. does so at the same time.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. rises with step and sign of E.A.) you will pass out our Candidate.
(I.G. discharges sign, goes to the door and opens it. Meanwhile, J.D. retrieves his wand, turns anti-clockwise and leads Can. to the door where the Tyler waits to receive Can. I.G. closes the door. J.D. and S.D. return to the North-West corner and both march smartly up the North. S.D. stands at his position at the N.E. corner. J.D. salutes with his wand in passing the W.M. along the East, up the South without saluting the J.W. and takes his position in the S.W. corner of the Lodge. Both Deacons place their wands in the stands and sit down in unison.)
(The Lodge is then opened in the Second Degree.)

sources.title: UGLE: Freemasonry questions and the three degrees

title: Fellow Craft: opening and passing
summary: Follow the second-degree opening, passing ceremony and examination.

sections.heading: Opening in the second degree
sections.body:
The Ceremony of Opening the Lodge in the Second Degree.
(The W.M. gives one knock, which is answered by the Wardens, and, rising, says-)
W. M. - Brethren, assist me to open the Lodge in the Second Degree. (All rise.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, (J.W. responds with step and sign of E.A.) what is the first care of every Fellow-Craft Freemason?
J. W. - To see that the Lodge is properly tyled.
W. M. - You will direct that duty to be done.
J. W. - (J.W. discharges sign) Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds with step and sign of E.A.) you will see that the Lodge is properly tyled.
(I.G. discharges sign, opens the door and looks out and then shuts the door.)
I. G. (with step and sign of E.A.)
Bro. Junior Warden, the lodge is properly tyled. (I.G. discharges sign)
J. W. (with step and sign of E.A.)
Worshipful Master, the Lodge is properly tyled. (J.W. discharges sign)
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, (S.W. responds with step and sign of E.A.) what is our next care ? S. W. - To see that the Brethren appear to order as Freemasons. (S.W. discharges sign)
W. M. - Brethren, to order as Freemasons in the First Degree. (All stand to order.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, are you a Fellow-Craft Freemason?
J. W. - I am, Worshipful Master; try me and prove me.
W. M. - By what instrument in Architecture will you be proved?
J. W. - By the Square.
W. M. - What is a Square?
J. W. - An angle of ninety degrees, or the fourth part of a circle.
W. M. - Being yourself acquainted with the proper mode, you will prove the Brethren to be Craftsmen, and will demonstrate that proof to me by copying their example.
J. W. - Brethren, it is the Worshipful Master's command that you prove yourselves to be Craftsmen. (All the Brethren present will prove themselves as F.C. except the W.M. and J.W.)
J. W. - Worshipful Master, the Brethren present have proved themselves Craftsmen, and in obedience to your command I thus copy their example. (Gives step and sign of F.C.)
W. M. - I acknowledge the correctness of the proof. (Gives step and sign of F.C.)
Chaplain - Brethren, before the Lodge is opened in the Second Degree, let us supplicate The Grand Geometrician Of The Universe, that the rays of Heaven may shed their benign influence over us, to enlighten us in the paths of Virtue and Science. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Brethren, I declare the Lodge duly opened upon the Square, for the instruction and improvement of Craftsmen.
(W.M. gives the knocks of a F.C. with his gavel, which the Wardens, I.G. and Tyler repeat. The J.D. goes to the Secretary’s table and the S.D. goes to the J.W.’s pedestal. I.P.M. goes straight to J.W.’s pedestal and cut in, to the centre of the Lodge under the ‘G’. Deacons take their places behind the I.P.M.. cross their wands with a click to signal the I.P.M. to walk to the W.M.’s pedestal escorted by the Deacons with wands crossed. I.P.M. kneels on his right knee and rearranges the Square and Compasses. I.P.M. salutes the W.M. as a F.C. and return to his seat. Deacons salute the W.M. with their wands and return to their respective positions and place their wands in the stands. J.D. opens the second degree tracing board.)
W. M. - Brethren, be seated.

sections.heading: Admission, examination and approach
sections.body:
The Ceremony of Passing to the Second Degree
(When the Can. is prepared, the Tyler gives the knock of the First Degree.***)
I. G. - (advances with step and sign of a F.C.) Bro. Junior Warden, there is an alarm. (I.G. discharges sign.)
J. W. - (rises with step and sign of a F.C.) Worshipful Master, there is an alarm. (J.W. holds sign.)
W. M. - Bro. Junior Warden, you will inquire the cause of that alarm. (J.W. discharges sign and sits down.)
J. W. - Bro. Inner Guard, (I.G. responds and holds sign of a F.C.) you will see who seeks admission.
(The I.G. discharges sign and opens the door.)
I. G. - (to Tyler) Whom have you there?
TY. - Bro. A. B., who has been regularly initiated into Freemasonry, and has made such progress therein as he hopes will entitle him to be passed to the Second Degree, for which Ceremony he is properly prepared.
I. G. - How does he hope to obtain the Privileges of the Second Degree?
TY. - By the help of God, the assistance of the Square, and the benefit of a Pass Word.
I. G. - (to Can.) You will give me the Pass Word. (Can. gives the Pass Grip and Pass Word to the I.G.)
I. G. - Let him wait while I report to the W.M. (I.G. closes the door.)
I. G. - (advances with step and sign of a F.C. and holds the sign.) Worshipful Master, at the door of the Lodge stands Bro. A. B., who has been regularly initiated into Freemasonry, and has made such progress therein as he hopes will entitle him to be passed to the Second Degree, for which Ceremony he is properly prepared.
W. M. - How does he hope to obtain the privileges of the Second Degree?
I. G. - By the help of God, the assistance of the Square, and the benefit of a Pass Word.
W. M. - We acknowledge the powerful aid by which he seeks admission; do you, Bro. Inner Guard, vouch that he is in possession of the Pass Word ?
I. G. - I do, Worshipful Master.
W. M. - Then let him be admitted in due form. (I.G. discharges sign.) Brother Deacons, you will attend the Candidate.
(The S.D. walks via the East, salutes the W.M. in passing, and South to the J.D.’s position. Both Deacons go to the door. I.G. opens the door.)
I. G. - You will advance to me with the step and sign of an E.A.
(Can. does so. I.G. applies the Square on the Can., and raises it above his head to show the W.M. that he has done so and steps back to the back of the S.W.’s chair. The S.D. takes the Can.'s right hand in his left, the J.D. on the other side, conducts the Can. to the N.W. corner of the Lodge.)
W. M. - Let the Candidate kneel, while the blessing of Heaven is invoked in aid of our proceedings.
(The Can. kneels and places his right palm over his left breast, the Deacons stand on either side, with their wands crossed so as to meet over the head of the Candidate)
W. M. - (gives one knock which the Wardens repeat) To order, Brethren. (all stand with the sign of fidelity)
Chaplain - We supplicate a continuance of Thine aid, O Merciful Lord, on behalf of ourselves and of him who kneels before Thee. May the work begun in Thy Name be continued to Thy Glory, and be evermore established in us by obedience to Thy Divine precepts. So Mote It Be.
W. M. - Let the Candidate rise and perambulate the Lodge.
Brethren, be seated.
(The S.D. instructs the Can. to rise, takes him by the right hand and leads him up the North, East, directs him to salute the W.M. as an E A. in passing, and stops in front of the J.W.’s pedestal.)
S. D. - You will advance to the J.W. with the step and sign of an E.A. (Can. does so. J.W. rises and replies with step and sign of an E.A.)
J. W. - Have you anything further to communicate?
CAN. - I have. (S.D. passes right hand of Can. to J.W., in order to give the E.A. grip.)
J. W. - What is this?
CAN. - The Grip or Token of an Entered Apprentice Freemason.
J. W. - What does this Grip demand?
CAN. - A Word.
J. W. - Being now in open Lodge, you may give me the Word freely and in full.
CAN. - B...
J. W. - Pass, B... (J.W. passes Can.’s right hand back to the S.D. and sits down.) (The Can. is conducted down the West and S.D. instructs him to salute the S.W. in passing as an E.A. S.D. and Can. halt at the N.W. corner of the Lodge. The W.M. gives one knock, which the S.W. and the J.W. answer.)
W. M. - The Brethren in the North, East, South, and West will take notice that Bro. A. B. is about to pass in view before them, to show that he is properly prepared to be passed to the Second Degree.
(He is again conducted round the Lodge, saluting the W.M. and the J.W. in passing as an E.A.; and stops in front of the S.W.’s pedestal.)
S. D. - You will advance to the S.W. with the step and sign of an E.A. and be prepared to give the Pass Grip and Pass Word leading from the First to the Second Degree which were communicated to you before you retired from the Lodge.
(Can. advances to the S.W. as an E.A.; S.W. rises and replies with the step and sign of an E.A.)
S. W. - Do you bring anything else?
CAN. - I do. (S.D. passes right hand of Can. to S.W., in order to give the P.G.)
S. W. - (rises) What is this?
CAN. - The Pass Grip, leading from the First to the Second Degree.
S. W. - To this Pass Grip a Word is attached, which I will thank you for.
CAN. - S.........
S. W. - What does this Word imply?
CAN. - An Ear of Corn or a Stream of Water.
S. W. - How is it depicted in a Fellow-Crafts’ lodge?
CAN. - By an Ear of Corn near a Stream of Water.
S. W. - What is the import of that symbol?
CAN. - P.....
S. W. - Pass, S......... - P.....
(S.W. passes Can.’s back to S.D. Can. is conducted to the left side of the S.W.’s pedestal and placed facing the W.M. The S.W. takes the Can. by the right hand in his own left.)
S. W. - (rises with sign of fidelity) Worshipful Master, I present to you Bro. A. B., a Candidate properly prepared to be passed to the Second Degree.
W. M. - Bro. Senior Warden, your presentation shall be attended to, for which purpose you will direct the Senior Deacon to instruct the Candidate to advance to the East by the proper steps.
(S.W. discharges sign and sits.)
S. W. - Brother Senior Deacon, it is the Worshipful Master’s command that you instruct the Can. to advance to the East by the proper steps.
(The S.D. conducts the Can. to the N.E. corner, and facing South.)
S. D. - The method of advancing from West to East in this Degree is by five steps, as though ascending a winding staircase. You will copy me.
(J.D. stays at the N.E. corner. S.D. steps off from the N.E. corner and by 5 knee high steps, advances to the centre front of the W.M.’s pedestal. Can. is assisted to copy the steps to the centre front of the W.M.’s pedestal. When Can. completes the steps, J.D. joins on the left of the Can. and the S.D. on the right, both one pace back.)

sections.heading: Obligation and the supplied explanations
sections.body:
W. M. - As the Secrets of each Degree are to be kept separate and distinct, another Obligation will now be required of you, in some respects similar to the one in the First Degree. Are you willing to take it?
CAN. - I am. (S.D. prompts, if necessary.)
W. M. - Then you will kneel on your right knee, place your right hand on the Volume of the Sacred Law while your left will rest upon the Square, and say after me, repeating your several names at length:
(The W.M. gives the one knock, which is answered by the Wardens: W.M. and all the Brethren rise, and stand with the Sign of Fidelity. Both Deacons cross their wands over the Can.’s head.)
W. M. - I, A. B., in the presence of The Grand Geometrician Of The Universe, and of this Worthy and Worshipful Lodge of Fellow- Craft Freemasons, lawfully constituted and regularly assembled, hereby (W.M. touches Can.’s right hand with his right hand) and hereon (W.M. touches the V.S.L. with his right hand and returns back to sign of fidelity) most solemnly and sincerely swear, that I will always hele, conceal, and never wilfully reveal any or either of the secrets or mysteries of, or at all belonging to, this Second Degree in Freemasonry, denominated the Fellow-Crafts’ Degree, to him who is but an Entered Apprentice, any more than I would reveal the secrets of either Degree to those of the popular and uninstructed world who are not Freemasons; except in the case of one who has duly served a full month as an Entered Apprentice, and has been presented a Candidate properly prepared to be passed to the Degree of Fellow-Craft, and then only in a Regular Lodge of Fellow-Craft Freemasons duly and properly opened upon the Square. I further solemnly promise to act upon the Square (here the W.M. touches the Square held by the Can.) as a true and faithful Craftsman, to answer signs, to obey summonses, and to maintain the principles inculcated in the First Degree. These several points I solemnly swear to observe without evasion, equivocation, or mental reservation of any kind, and I pray to The Grand Geometrician Of The Universe that he will keep me steadfast in this Great and Solemn Obligation of a Fellow Craft Freemason.
(W.M. removes the Square from the Can.’s left hand while the Can.’s right hand remains on the V.S.L.)
W. M. - As a pledge of your Fidelity to this solemn Obligation, you will seal it upon the Volume of the Sacred Laws twice with your lips. (Can. kisses the VSL twice. W.M. and all the Brethren discharge the sign of fidelity. Deacons uncross wands.) Your progress in Freemasonry is indicated by the relative position of the Square and the Compasses. When you were made an Entered Apprentice, both points of the Compasses were concealed; (W.M. points but do not touch the Square and Compasses) in this Degree one is disclosed, implying that you are now midway in Freemasonry, superior to an Entered Apprentice, but inferior to the position to which we trust you will attain in due time. (W.M. takes him by the right hand.) Rise, duly Obligated Probationer in the Second Degree. (W.M. passes hand to S.D.)
W. M. - Brethren, be seated.
(J.D. conducts Can. along the East, South, West and North to the North-East corner, and places Can. facing South. The W.M. descends from the dais and stands on the South side of the Lodge, facing the Can.)
W. M. - Now that you have taken the Solemn Obligation of a Fellow-Craft Freemason, I will entrust you with the Secrets of this Degree. You will first advance to me as an Entered Apprentice, giving me the Sign of that Degree. (Can. shows step and sign of E.A., W.M. replies with same step and sign) You will now take another Short Pace forward with your Left Foot, (W.M. demonstrates and instructs simultaneously) bringing your Right Heel into the Hollow of the Left Foot as before. That is the Second Regular Step in Freemasonry, (Can. and W.M. keep standing in the 2nd Regular Step) and it is in this position that the Secrets of this Degree are communicated. They consist, as in the First Degree, of a Sign, a Grip or Token and a Word with this difference, that the Sign in this Degree is Threefold or may be separated into three several Signs. The first is given thus : place your right hand on the left breast with the thumb extended in the form of a square. (W.M. instructs Can. to copy and both maintain the sign) It is called the
S... of F......., or the S........ S... emblematically to Shield the Heart the repository of our Secrets from the attacks of the insidious. The second is given thus : Throw up the left hand with upper arm horizontal from the shoulder to the elbow, and lower arm perpendicular from the elbow to the finger tips with the thumb extended in the form of a square. (W.M. instructs Can. to copy and both maintain the sign) It is called the H....... S... or S... of P............ This is said to have been the Sign used by Joshua when fighting the battles of the Lord ‘in the going down to Beth-horon’. In this position he spake those memorable words, ‘Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies’. This is the P.... S... : imagine holding a sharp instrument with the thumb and the first finger of the right hand, make a cutting motion downwards over the heart, grab the heart out, throw it across and downward to the right side, and return the right hand to the breast as before. (W.M. instructs Can. to copy and then both maintain the sign) It alludes to the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree and implied that as a man of honour and a Fellow-Craft Freemason you would rather have your left breast laid open (W.M. demonstrates as he explains and instructs Can. to copy in synchronisation.) and your heart torn therefrom and given as prey to the ravenous birds of the air or the devouring beasts of the field than willingly or knowingly violate the Solemn Obligation of a Fellow- Craft Freemason. (W.M. and Can. discharge F.C. sign) The Grip or Token of a Fellow Craft is given by a distinct pressure of the thumb on the second joint of the hand. (W.M. demonstrates) To this Grip a Word is attached, one with which you will observe the same strict caution as with the one in the First Degree, namely, by never giving it at length but always lettering or halving it, except in open Lodge and for the instruction of a Candidate. Being now in open Lodge, I will, for your instruction, repeat the Word in full; it is J...... As you will shortly be called upon for this Grip and Word, the Senior Deacon will now give the answers which you will then be expected to give for yourself. (S.D. takes up position at right angle to Can. and facing East.)
W. M. - What is this?
