sections.heading: Mixed and changing emotional responses
sections.body:
Emotions
The experience of work is saturated with a variety of emotions – from frustration, happiness, anxiety or fear, to an enduring sense of dissatisfaction or commitment.
Emotions will shape the anticipation, the experience and the aftermath of change.
Change can create a mix of emotions – simultaneously positive and negative. Change can be a threat or an opportunity, a cause of concern or celebration, surprising or predictable, controlled or uncontrolled.
Leading and managing people along a transformational journey demands the ability to recognize how and why people will react emotionally.
Types of emotions
Emotions can be classified as positive - excitement, enthusiasm, happiness, confidence - or negative – guilt, anger, frustration, sadness, worry, anxiety.
Positive emotions can stimulate the desire to generate broader ways of thinking, improve decision-making, create an open mind about future possibilities.
Conversely, negative emotions can create a narrow way of thinking, withdrawal from participating in meetings and decision-making, criticism about future options.
During organizational change individuals will experience both types of emotions simultaneously. Emotions will vary over time.

sections.heading: Emotional display, suppression and emotional labour
sections.body:
Suppressing and expressing emotions
Organizations can shape and control the way that their employees display emotions. Jennifer Talvar (2002) describes how managers in McDonald’s invent ways of stimulating employees’ emotions so that negative feelings are suppressed. For example, managers constantly remind employees to "leave your problems at home".
This can lead to burnout, exhaustion, low job satisfaction, absenteeism and conflict.
Emotional labour describes when individuals manage their emotions within an organization in exchange for a salary, to meet the requirements of their job (especially customer-facing jobs).
During a change initiative emotional labour may be required by managers and employees who feel the need to hide their feelings about the change in case their expression is construed as an unwelcome form of resistance.
Such emotional labour can have a positive impact on employees’ performance (increase in sales…) and personal welfare. On the negative side, when there is a disparity between an individual’s felt and displayed emotion, emotional dissonance might occur.
They shape the way that emotion is to be displayed as well as the labour that goes into making it look good – the emotional labour (Hochschild, 1983)

sections.heading: Emotional intelligence and self-awareness
sections.body:
Emotional Intelligence (EQ)
The ability of managers and leaders to recognize and manage emotions in themselves and in other people is known as emotional intelligence (Goleman, 1995).
Salovey and Mayer (1990) defines it as "the ability to monitor one's own and others’ feelings and emotions, to discriminate among them and to use this information to guide ones' thinking and actions"
It is based on an individual’s own self-awareness. It is not fixed for life and may be improved with suitable training.
Part of leading and managing people through change is being able to acknowledge and understand complex and evolving emotions.

sections.heading: Order, responsibility and outlook
sections.body:
Ctrl: The Handler
Congratulations. You rolled one of the rarest personalities in the SBTI universe. CTRL people look like they were born with a task manager installed straight into their nervous system. What ordinary people call 'rules' feels like factory settings to you; what ordinary people call 'planning' looks more like a rough doodle compared with the way your brain arranges reality. Having a CTRL around is like having an emergency Ctrl+S key living next to you. Right before someone’s life starts derailing, CTRL will archive the chaos, restore the correct version, and drag the whole situation back on track with logic too clean to argue with. In a collapsing universe, they are the last reboot button still glowing.
ATM-er: The Walking ATM
ATM-er does not necessarily mean throwing cash everywhere. It means always being the one who pays. Paying with time, paying with emotional bandwidth, paying with patience, paying with a night that should have belonged to peace and sleep. Other people insert panic and trouble into you like a card into an old but reliable machine, and what comes out is the receipt that says, 'It’s okay, I’ve got this.' Your life is a grand one-person checkout lane that nobody applauds, powered by a responsibility complex that simply refuses to clock out.
Dior-s: The Cynic Sage
You are not merely a loser archetype. You are the spiritually misplaced heir of Diogenes himself. Dior-s personalities don’t reject ambition because they are lazy; they reject it because they’ve already seen that the endgame of conventional 'success' is often just a more expensive prison. When other people chase trends and get tossed around by the era, Dior-s is sunbathing in a barrel of their own making, perfectly at peace. Their philosophy is brutally practical: lying down is often more comfortable than standing up, and when it’s mealtime, you eat. Simple. Tested. True.
Boss: The Boss
BOSS is the kind of person who reaches for the steering wheel even when the tank is almost empty and the navigation app is clearly hallucinating. You say 'I’ll drive,' and somehow the car still reaches the destination. Efficiency is not a preference here. It is doctrine. Order is not a hobby. It is oxygen. BOSS personalities don’t merely have leadership aura; they generate the aura itself. Within a few meters, the air gets more serious and more productive. What normal people call self-improvement, they often treat like warm-up stretches before the real work begins.
Than-K: The Thanker
THAN-K people possess a supernatural ability to turn irritation into gratitude with terrifying speed. Traffic jam? Excellent, now there is more time to listen to this beautiful song and study the anxious faces outside the window. Bad weather? Wonderful, now the universe has offered a new angle from which to appreciate existence. Their softness is real, but so is their power. A THAN-K friend is like carrying around a renewable energy tower that runs on perspective and grace. Even mildew in the corner of a wall can become a Van Gogh sky if they are the one describing it.
Oh-No!: The Alarmist
To the OH-NO personality, 'oh no' is not panic. It is advanced cognition. When ordinary people see a glass near the edge of a table, OH-NO sees the full cinematic franchise: spilled water, short circuit, fire, building evacuation, financial loss, butterfly effect, apocalypse. Then, with a single sacred 'oh no,' they move the glass to the center of the table and place a coaster under it for good measure. They respect boundaries and risk with almost religious intensity. They are the straight-backed guardians of order in a world that keeps trying to slip on its own banana peel.

sections.heading: Action, affection and social presentation
sections.body:
GoGo: The Go-Goer
GOGO people live in an extreme what-you-see-is-what-you-get reality. Their life philosophy is beautifully savage: if I close my eyes, then it’s dark; if I spend all my money, then I clearly have no money left; if I’m standing on the crosswalk, then I am now a pedestrian. Flawless loop. Impossible to debate. While others are still dissecting a problem, GOGO has already turned the chicken and the egg into one decisive over-rice combo and called the issue solved. They do not 'process complexity.' They delete pending tasks.
Sexy: The Heartthrob
When you enter a room, the lighting system seems to identify you as the focal subject and quietly lower the brightness to save electricity. When you smile, the humidity in the room drops because all the water vapor has condensed into heart shapes inside other people’s eyes. SEXY personalities do not always need effortful performance. Their existence itself behaves like a dramatic essay written in expensive perfume. If enough SEXY types gathered in one place, it would not be shocking if time itself slowed down a little just to admire the scene.
Love-R: The Lover
LOVE-R is the emotional endangered species that somehow survived into the algorithm age. Your inner processor is not binary. It runs in rainbow mode. A single falling leaf does not say 'autumn' to you; it opens a thirteen-act tragedy about fate, sacrifice, renewal, and silent devotion. Your inner world feels like an amusement park that never closes, and somewhere deep inside it is a constant search for the one person who can read the map, understand the rides, and stay beside you until the universe turns its lights off.
Mum: The Mom Friend
MUM energy existed before language, before clocks, before the first star burped itself into the sky. The core color of this personality is gentleness. They notice emotion fast, read atmosphere well, and often know exactly when to stop, when to comfort, and when to tell themselves, 'It’s okay, let it go.' MUM types are natural healers of other people’s sadness. The only tragic detail is that when they cry, the dosage of kindness they prescribe to themselves is often smaller than the dosage they freely hand to everyone else.
Fake: The Masker
In social situations, FAKE personalities switch masks faster than most people switch keyboards. One second it is heart-to-heart bestie mode, next second the boss walks in and the reliable-professional mask snaps into place with showroom-level polish. You thought you found someone who truly understood you? Maybe you simply met an extraordinarily high-performance imitation life-form. The late-night horror of the FAKE personality is that when every mask finally comes off, what remains underneath may feel alarmingly empty, because the masks were the structure all along.
OJBK: The Whatever
OJBK is no longer just a personality. It is a system of governance. While ordinary mortals burn precious brain cells deciding whether to eat rice or noodles for lunch, the OJBK personality glances over the entire human dilemma and delivers an imperial decree: 'Whatever.' This is not indecision. This is scale. They are quietly informing you that your tiny earthly choices do not qualify as meaningful events in the empire. They do not argue because arguing with protozoa about the destiny of the universe is beneath the throne.

sections.heading: Chaos, humor, analysis and deadlines
sections.body:
Malo - The Chaos Monkey
Friend, you are not 'young at heart.' You simply never completed the full human upgrade. Your spirit still hangs from a tree, thrilled by simple joy and suspicious of civilization. When humanity came down from the branches, learned to stand upright, and started wearing ties to meetings, the MALO ancestor stayed above them, scratched their butt, and made a dismissive little monkey sound. MALO understands something most people forget: civilization is often a boring pay-to-win game. Rules can be broken, ceilings can be climbed, and meeting rooms can absolutely be used for backflips.
Joke-r: The Jester
JOKE-R is less a person and more a clown wearing another clown wearing another joke. Peel back one layer and there is a bit. Peel back another and there is a punchline. Keep opening and eventually you hit the empty center, where only a tiny echo remains saying, 'Ha. Didn’t expect that, huh?' JOKE-Rs are the designated mood crew of every social gathering. With them around, the room does not go cold. The loudest laugh often comes from them too, because sometimes the biggest laugh is simply the most efficient way to cover the sound of a fracture inside.
WOC!: The Whoa Person
WOC! personalities run on two separate operating systems. The surface system exists to produce highly expressive sound effects like 'holy crap,' 'no way,' and 'what?!' The background system stays calm, cool, and deeply unsurprised: yes, that tracks, exactly as expected. WOC! types are usually not interested in unnecessary meddling. They know that explaining logic to an idiot is like trying to plaster a wall with mud: exhausting, degrading, and somehow you still end up dirty. So instead they grip a blade of wise grass and honor the absurd world with one heartfelt, perfectly timed 'WOC!'
Thin-K: The Thinker
THIN-K brains are built differently. Your mind seems to run in continuous analysis mode. Information is not simply received; it is interrogated, cross-examined, and logged together with its logic chain, hidden bias profile, and background report on the author’s ideological ancestors. In an age of information overload, you are not easily carried away. You weigh costs and benefits in relationships, guard your mental space fiercely, and when other people think you are spacing out alone, what is actually happening is an internal filing operation of terrifying sophistication.
Shit: The Malcontent
SHIT personalities are walking paradox engines. Mouth: 'This project is garbage.' Hands: quietly open Excel and build a full model plus gantt chart. Mouth: 'These coworkers are all unbearable.' Hands: stay up late cleaning the entire mess after everyone else fumbles it. Mouth: 'The world is crap. Burn it down.' Body: wakes up at seven the next morning and squeezes into a miserable commute to keep the machine running anyway. Do not confuse the profanity with surrender. That alarm sound is actually the trumpet announcing that they are about to save the world again, resentfully and efficiently.
Zzzz: The Snoozer
A ZZZZ type can ignore ninety-nine unread messages in the group chat with saint-level stillness. But once someone sends 'deadline in thirty minutes' with an @everyone attached, they rise like a mummy cracking open a stone tomb, type a slow 'received,' and then somehow submit a passable result in twenty-nine minutes. This personality does not truly awaken until the highest-authority command appears: the deadline itself. Until that exact moment, nothing moves. Once it hits, the legendary last-second surge arrives and proves a cosmic principle: sometimes the best way to avoid doing something wrong is to do absolutely nothing until panic becomes fuel.

sections.heading: Focus, solitude, intensity and other narratives
sections.body:
Poor: The Specialist
POOR does not mean your wallet got sentenced. It means your desires have gone through ruthless downsizing. While other people scatter their attention like QR codes all over the sky, you compress yours into a single laser beam. The world of POOR is simple: irrelevant things get muted, important things get drilled hard. Noise, vanity, social performance, random networking? Sorry, no bandwidth. It may look like scarcity from the outside, but in practice it is concentration so intense it starts to resemble mining equipment.
Monk: The Monk
While other people scream their love songs inside a KTV room, MONK is at home studying a higher path. This personality has already half-left the mortal world and does not appreciate random visitors disturbing their cultivation. Personal space is not a preference to MONK. It is a barrier field, a sacred mountain, an absolute domain. Enter at your own risk. They do not cling because their worldview assumes everything deserves its own orbit. If planets can love each other while staying millions of miles apart, why should humans insist on breathing directly into one another’s souls?
Solo: The Loner
SOLO personalities often keep their self-worth low and their defenses high. Instead of reaching outward, they sometimes step back first and build a long wall around the soul that says, in very bold letters, 'Do not come closer.' Every brick in that wall used to be a wound. SOLO is the hedgehog that hides every soft spot and points its sharpest spines at the world. Those spikes are not only aggression. They are also unsent messages saying, 'Please don’t come near, I’m afraid you’ll get hurt too,' and at the exact same time, 'Please don’t leave.'
Fuck: The Wild One
Somewhere inside human civilization lives a humanoid weed that no herbicide can kill. That is the FUCK personality. In their worldview, polite social rules are frequently meaningless, and their emotional switch is not digital but physical: it flips directly between FUCK YEAH and FUCK OFF. They are not chasing only instant pleasure. They are chasing raw vitality, the feeling of being fully alive while their blood seems to ram through every wall in the body. When everyone else has been tamed into well-behaved domestic birds, FUCK is still the last wolf howl coming from the wilderness.
Dead: The Deadpan
The DEAD personality is not simply low-energy. It feels more like someone who already completed every main quest, side quest, hidden quest, deleted the save file, restarted nine hundred and ninety-nine times, and eventually realized the game itself was never all that interesting. They look at the world with the tired calm of a post-desire sage. This is what happens when somebody stops investing faith in every fake source of urgency and no longer sees meaning in most of the noise. Their existence becomes a silent, elegant protest against the entire overclocked modern circus.
IMFW: The Fragile One
IMFW is not ordinary weakness. It is a rare and hyper-sensitive personality type with brittle pride, thin safety walls, and a heart that is far more serious than it looks. Because of that, IMFW can locate the strongest Wi-Fi signal in any room, meaning the single person they instinctively trust the most. Walking into an IMFW life is like entering a high-end orchid greenhouse: the temperature, humidity, and daily verbal photosynthesis of 'I care about you' all matter. Give them one piece of candy and they may answer with a pair of shining eyes full of trust. Maybe you are not useless at all. Maybe you are simply too undefended.
HHHH: The Goofball
Congratulations. Your mental wiring is so novel that the standard personality library has collapsed in protest. HHHH is only assigned when your highest normal-type match drops below sixty percent, meaning the system itself has more or less thrown up its hands and said, 'I genuinely have no proper drawer for this person.' What qualities define HHHH? Hahahahahahaha. Sorry, that really is most of the official documentation. You can still inspect the fifteen dimensions for an extremely unofficial reading, but the honest truth is that your brain arrived through a side door the original framework forgot to build for.
Drun-k: The Drunkard
Why are you walking like the ground is moving? Why are your emotions permanently overclocked? Why does the world come with built-in double vision? Because what runs through your veins is not blood but premium baijiu. DRUNK is the hidden route where ethanol takes over the operating system and skips the ordinary trial altogether. Perhaps you have already reached the point of pouring liquor into a thermos and drinking it like water. Alcohol turns you into a banquet philosopher, a nightclub poet, a flaming sun at the center of the table. Then ten in the morning arrives, your head splits like a walnut, food crumbs cling to the corner of your mouth, and your soul retreats into a dark little corner. At last you understand that last night’s heroic orator has officially become a drunkard.

sections.heading: Eleven portfolio and exposure descriptions
sections.body:
Portfolio
Various Utility Functions
Portfolios constructed to maximize an investor's satisfaction or utility, taking into account their specific risk tolerance and return preferences.
Neutral
Portfolios designed to minimize exposure to certain risk factors or biases, ensuring they are not overly affected by market movements or specific risks.
Dollar-Neutral
Portfolios that balance long and short positions to equalize the dollar value of investments, aiming to neutralize exposure to market direction and focus on relative performance.
Beta-neutral
Portfolios are structured to have a beta of zero, meaning they aim to eliminate sensitivity to overall market movements, focusing instead on generating returns from stock-specific factors.
Optimal equitization
The process of converting cash or cash-equivalent holdings into a balanced portfolio of equities to achieve the desired level of market exposure and enhance returns.
Long/Short Equity
A strategy that involves buying (long) stocks expected to increase in value and selling (short) stocks expected to decrease, aiming to profit from the relative performance of the chosen securities.
Market-Neutral
A strategy that seeks to neutralize market risk by balancing long and short positions so that overall exposure to market movements is minimized, focusing on profiting from stock-specific factors.
Equitized
A strategy that involves converting a non-equity investment, such as cash or bonds, into a position in equities to gain market exposure and potential returns while managing risks associated with the equity market.
130-30
A strategy where investors take a long position in preferred stocks worth 130% of their portfolio’s value and simultaneously short stocks worth 30%, leveraging the portfolio to enhance returns while maintaining a net 100% market exposure.
Momentum Trading
A strategy that involves buying securities that have shown upward price trends and selling those with downward trends, based on the expectation that these trends will continue for a certain period.
Hedge
A risk management strategy used to offset potential losses in one investment by taking an opposite position in a related asset, effectively reducing exposure to adverse market movements.

How financial decisions are made: objective information (history & current) → perceived information (interpretation) → information processing (satisfactory & self-deception) → decisions (buy/sell/hold) → activation (procrastination) → action

sections.heading: Arithmetic average and compounded change
sections.body: In the source’s illustrative +10% then −10% example, an amount of 100 becomes 110 and then 99. The arithmetic average return is zero, but the cumulative change is −1%. Reversing those two returns also ends at 99 if no money is added or withdrawn. This is an arithmetic illustration, not historical investment performance.

sections.heading: The Super Bowl market story
sections.body:
Concept clarified
This is a spurious-correlation warning, not a forecasting rule. Team identity has no investment mechanism established by the note; data mining and out-of-sample failure must be considered.
Super bowl effect
A Super Bowl win by an NFC team predicts a rise in the stock market for that year.

sections.heading: Calendar and announcement anomalies
sections.body:
Concept clarified
Time-of-day, weekday, month-turn, holiday and late-reporting patterns are hypotheses requiring a defined dataset, period, market, costs and out-of-sample checks. The stated last-two/first-three-day window is source wording, not a current reliable trading signal. “Weekend reporting causes” is stronger than the evidence supplied.
Time-of-the-day effect
Returns and volatility can vary depending on the time of the trading day.
Day-of-the-week effect
Weekend reporting causes bad Friday-to-Monday returns.
Week-of-the-month effect
Returns may vary depending on the specific week within a month.
Turn-of-the-month effect
Stock prices increased during the last two days and the first three days of each month.
Holiday Effect
Stock market to gain on the final trading day before an exchange-mandated long weekend.
Late reporter anomaly
Late announcements are often negative and cause a price decline.

title: Pitch-deck foundations: explain the problem, offer and opportunity
summary: Use six supplied sections to prepare a clear story about a problem, solution, product, market, competitors and team.

sections.heading: Problem: relevance, examples and evidence
sections.body:
Pitch Deck
Problem
Talk about the problem you are l trying to solve and why this is relevant
Tell a short story about a real person that experienced the problem (example)
Show an easy explanation of the problem you are addressing
If possible, explain the problem showing relevant numbers
If you are not solving a new problem, you may want to present the opportunity slide instead of the problem slide

sections.heading: Solution: a realistic response to the problem
sections.body:
Solution
Always try to present the solution of your problem realistically and innovatively
If it is a physical solution, show prototypes or the product itself
If it is a digital solution, show videos, graphics or demo of the product
Talk about how your problem can be solved with the solution proposed

sections.heading: Product: demonstrate what the offer does
sections.body:
Product
Use this slide to describe your product or service in detail
Add screenshots. mockups, videos, and the essential features of your product
Everything you have to explain about your
The product is helpful and demonstrates that your idea is viable and competitive
Be careful not to repeat the content of the solution slide

sections.heading: Market: scale, characteristics and sources
sections.body:
Market
Give specific numbers about how big your company can get
Total addressable market (TAM) & serviceable available market (SAM) & serviceable obtainable market (SOM)
Explain special characteristics of the market (e.G. long sales cycles)
Always show and add the sources regarding the collected numbers
If you have a growing demand in your market, add the growth figures
If you are in a new market, try to make analogies with similar markets

sections.heading: Competitors: alternatives and differentiation
sections.body:
Competitor
List all major competitors in your market using graphics
Describe what your competitors do well and what they do poorly
Show what distinguishes you from these competitors and where you see your position in the market (USP)

sections.heading: Team: relevant experience and responsibilities
sections.body:
Team
Present a short bio and the role for each of your key team members
Always try to add pictures of the respective team members
Present the education, relevant experience, and any accomplishments of the team members
